summary: Only the top 30 feet of North Baldy's 41-ft R-6 tower moved to Big Meadow Lake in 1989 as a wildlife observation tower; the rest was torn down.

facts.design: Top 30 ft of the 41-ft treated timber R-6 flat-roof tower built on North Baldy in 1964
facts.status_note: Only the top 30 feet of the 41-foot North Baldy tower came here; the rest was torn down in 1989.

access.note: Scenic Washington describes the lake as a visitor site with a boat launch, fishing pier and overnight camping. WillhiteWeb found the tower's access closed during one visit because of vandalism; the date is not given.

corrections.current: The tower still stands, but its cab is gone (FFLA).
corrections.proposed: Only the top 30 feet of the 41-foot North Baldy tower came to Big Meadow Lake as a wildlife observation tower; the rest was torn down in 1989.
corrections.why: The register, Kemnow's page and WillhiteWeb all say the tower was torn down in 1989 and only its top section was moved. The FFLA cab note was not checked against a source read here.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 1928 and firelookout.com gives 1925. Not resolved; the story reports both.

notes_for_editor: The brief's status note (FFLA: the tower stands but its cab is gone) is not confirmed by any source read here. The sources say only the top 30 feet moved, and none says what happened to the cab; the story says so. The 'relocated' event has no year in the brief; 1989 is from the register. The original us-wa-north-baldy record still says 'relocated' and only notes a move. It should get a 1989 teardown event and a note that only the top 30 feet moved. Cupola-cabin date (1928 register vs 1925 firelookout.com) is open. The access note is undated, so the closure may no longer apply.
